sourceChecks.location: Iris: colored part controlling pupil size
sourceChecks.claim: What is the colored part of the eye surrounding the pupil called? Answer: Iris. It changes pupil size and helps regulate how much light enters the eye. Adaptation: Global-MMLU, Cohere Labs et al., Apache 2.0.

reviewNotes: NEI identifies the iris as colored tissue controlling pupil size. Cornea is transparent, retina light-sensitive tissue and lens focusing tissue; all are eye structures. Source's Russian 'ирис/ученик' and unrelated cochlea distractor are corrected.

sourceChecks.location: Opening: two bean-shaped organs, one on each side of spine
sourceChecks.claim: Which of these organs is paired in typical human anatomy? Answer: Kidney. Two kidneys lie on opposite sides of the spine and filter blood. Adaptation: Global-MMLU, Cohere Labs et al., Apache 2.0.

reviewNotes: NIDDK explicitly describes two kidneys on opposite sides of the spine. Liver, stomach and gallbladder are unpaired in typical anatomy. 'Typical/обычное строение' avoids claiming everyone has two kidneys; source's mistranslated 'пару А' removed.

sourceChecks.location: Opening: ureters carry urine to bladder for storage
sourceChecks.claim: In which organ is urine stored before leaving the body? Answer: Urinary bladder. Urine reaches this organ from the kidneys through the ureters.

reviewNotes: NIDDK states urine flows via ureters into the bladder for storage. Gallbladder stores bile; stomach and pancreas do not store urine. RU uses мочеточники, not мочеиспускательный канал, matching EN ureters.

sourceChecks.claim: How many chambers does a normal human heart have? Answer: 4. The two upper chambers are atria and the two lower chambers are ventricles.

sourceChecks.location: Air fills your lung’s air sacs; Oxygen flows into your blood
sourceChecks.claim: What are the tiny air sacs in the lungs where gas exchange occurs called? Answer: Alveoli. Across their walls, oxygen enters the blood and carbon dioxide moves from blood into air. Adaptation: Global-MMLU, Cohere Labs et al., Apache 2.0.

reviewNotes: NHLBI confirms air sacs at bronchiole ends and oxygen/CO2 exchange with surrounding capillaries. Changed original to ask for air sacs: capillaries also participate in exchange but are blood vessels, so cannot be second correct answer. Bronchi and bronchioles are tubes.

sourceChecks.claim: Which fluid-filled structure in the inner ear has a spiral shape? Answer: Cochlea. It contains sensory hair cells that help detect sound.

reviewNotes: NIDCD steps 3–4 explicitly identify the fluid-filled snail-shaped cochlea and sensory hair cells. Eardrum, auditory tube and pinna are neither this inner-ear structure nor spiral fluid-filled sensory organ. Russian улитка and English cochlea refer to the same structure.

sourceChecks.claim: Which of these structures is part of the small intestine? Answer: Ileum. It is the final section, following the duodenum and jejunum. Adaptation: Global-MMLU, Cohere Labs et al., Apache 2.0.

sourceChecks.location: How do my kidneys work? Nephron includes glomerulus and tubule
sourceChecks.claim: What is the kidney unit in which blood is filtered and urine is formed called? Answer: Nephron. It includes a glomerulus and a tubule that returns needed substances to the blood.

reviewNotes: NIDDK explicitly names nephron as kidney filtering unit including glomerulus and tubule returning needed substances. Neuron, alveolus and osteon are structural units of other tissues. Both locales ask a unit, not the whole kidney or a single glomerulus.
